subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose first-class bootstrap selectors and dynamic command expansion for session context, and what security boundary should command-expanded bootstrap content use?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config/API behavior and could make workspace prompt files execute commands before every session, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Selector API first
options.body: Add a narrow maintained bootstrap tier/selector contract and defer command expansion until a separate sandbox/provenance design is approved.

options.title: Hook-only context
options.body: Route dynamic per-session context through documented hooks and keep core bootstrap loading limited to safe built-in files.

options.title: Full command expansion
options.body: Pursue bootstrap command expansion only with explicit opt-in, sandboxing, provenance, docs, and tests across session types.

recommendation.title: Selector API first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow maintained bootstrap tier/selector contract and defer command expansion until a separate sandbox/provenance design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for subagent bootstrap limiting and bootstrap resolution is in this path, and the remaining choice needs product/API boundary ownership.
